target_customer: Young Indian consumers who would invest spare change in digital gold and mutual funds
problem: Many Indian millennials do not invest for lack of time, knowledge or capital; the app rounds each digital payment up to the nearest 10 rupees and invests the difference.
business_model: Fee of 1.75 percent of assets under management, with planned bank partnerships (YC description)

founders.name: Gaurav Arora
founders.background_notes: YC page: full stack product builder across fintech and AI, says Spenny scaled to 500,000 users and exited.

exit.reason: Acquihire; the app was sunset and the team joined CRED

technical_complexity.rationale: Card and UPI transaction aggregation plus mutual fund and gold integrations; standard fintech engineering with regulatory registration needs.

defensibility.rationale: The round-up idea is easy to copy and distribution through banks was only planned.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search summaries list Jar, Groww and Zerodha Coin as later round-up adopters; undated and low reliability. CRED took the team in June 2023.

market_need_then: YC description claims 3,000 users and $15,000 in assets under management at Winter 2020 and cites UPI growth; these are company claims.

branding.domain_note: Uses spennyapp.com, with app suffix; no history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly saving language: save every time you spend, automatically

branding.brand_signature: Piggy bank (gullak) theme in the 'Bharat Ki Gullak' campaign, per a search summary
branding.community_and_virality: Brand campaign around the childhood gullak; site claims 400,000+ users, company claim.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly coinage and an Indian piggy bank campaign, but little independent press on the brand and the app was sunset.

outcome_analysis: Spenny launched a round-up investing app in India and claims about 400,000 users, but no priced funding round was verified. In June 2023 CRED acquihired the team after the app was being phased out, for an undisclosed amount. The outcome reads as a soft landing rather than a venture scale exit.
notes: YC directory says Active but its own page notes the CRED acquisition on June 23, 2023, so the status conflicts with the acquisition. The acquirer and acquihire framing come from search result summaries of Inc42, YourStory and Indian Startup News; the YourStory article returned 403 and was not opened, and Inc42 was not opened. Press names Rathin Shah as a co-founder and CEO who joined CRED, with JP Morgan Chase and BITS Pilani background in a search summary, but no company page or YC page opened names him, so he is not listed above. Funding is aggregator only and conflicting ($150,000, $200,000 or $1.26 million); none recorded. The company site said 400,000 users while the YC page says 500,000. Round-up competitors are undated, so the list is empty.
